name: Marak Ube-Black Sesame Cream
description: An unlicensed street-brand cream soda that has developed a fierce cult following, mixing synth-ube with real black sesame paste emulsified into a frothy, richly colored carbonated drink. Bottled in repurposed industrial containers with hand-applied labels.
flavor_profile: Deep, earthy nuttiness from black sesame balanced against the sweet, vanilla-adjacent purple yam; thick mouthfeel for a soda, with a roasted finish
cultural_context: Marak is passed hand to hand, not sold in stores. You know someone who knows the Marak guy. It's become a symbol of Shelf pride — the product is genuinely excellent, which makes the corporate beverage industry quietly furious. Vantage Consumer Group has attempted to buy the formula twice. Both times, the answer was reportedly unprintable.
story_hooks: The 'Marak guy' is actually a collective of three siblings operating out of a flooded sub-basement in the Shelf — one of them has just been approached by a Tier 4 restaurateur who wants to serve Marak at Φ18 a glass, and the family is divided on what to do.

A batch of Marak has been seized by Meridian 88 municipal enforcement citing 'unlicensed food production' — but the timing, right before a major labor vote, feels political, and someone wants the story told.

The black sesame paste in Marak is sourced from a vertical farm that is technically owned by a corponation shell entity — the collective doesn't know, but someone does, and is about to use it as leverage.
